claim: Biological and living systems process information across spatiotemporal scales, exhibiting the hallmark ability to constantly modulate their behavior to ever-changing and complex environments.
source_text: Biological and living systems process information across spatiotemporal scales, exhibiting the hallmark ability to constantly modulate their behavior to ever-changing and complex environments.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general statement about biological systems that draws from established scientific understanding of biological information processing.

claim: In the presence of repeated stimuli, a distinctive response is the progressive reduction of the activity at both sensory and molecular levels, known as habituation.
source_text: In the presence of repeated stimuli, a distinctive response is the progressive reduction of the activity at both sensory and molecular levels, known as habituation.
evidence_reasoning: This defines habituation as an established phenomenon in biology, supported by scientific consensus and referenced throughout the manuscript with citations.

claim: The minimal microscopic model recapitulates the main features of habituation, such as spontaneous recovery, potentiation, subliminal accumulation, and input sensitivity.
source_text: We show that our model recapitulates the main features of habituation, such as spontaneous recovery, potentiation, subliminal accumulation, and input sensitivity.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by computational simulations and analysis presented in the manuscript, particularly in Figure 2.

claim: An intermediate level of habituation is associated with a steep increase in information.
source_text: We find that an intermediate level of habituation is associated with a steep increase in information.
evidence_reasoning: This is a key finding derived from the computational analysis of mutual information in the model, shown in Figure 3.

claim: The region of maximal information gain can be characterized in terms of an optimal trade-off between information and energy consumption.
source_text: In particular, we are able to characterize this region of maximal information gain in terms of an optimal trade-off between information and energy consumption.
evidence_reasoning: This is derived from Pareto optimization analysis presented in Figure 4, combining information-theoretic and thermodynamic calculations.

claim: The model captures the main components of observed neural habituation in zebrafish larvae subjected to repeated looming stimulations.
source_text: We test our dynamical predictions against experimentally recorded neural responses in a zebrafish larva subjected to repeated looming stimulations, showing that our model captures the main components of the observed neural habituation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from zebrafish recordings compared with model predictions, shown in Figures 1d and 6.

claim: Sensing mechanisms in biological systems span a wide range of temporal and spatial scales, from cellular to multi-cellular level.
source_text: Sensing mechanisms in biological systems span a wide range of temporal and spatial scales, from cellular to multi-cellular level, forming the basis for decision-making and the optimization of limited resources
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about biological sensing, supported by multiple citations (Tkačik and Bialek, 2016; Azeloglu and Iyengar, 2015; etc.).

claim: Emergent macroscopic phenomena such as adaptation and habituation reflect the ability of living systems to effectively process the information they collect from their noisy environment.
source_text: Emergent macroscopic phenomena such as adaptation and habituation reflect the ability of living systems to effectively process the information they collect from their noisy environment
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by citations to theoretical work (Nemenman, 2012; Nakajima, 2015; Koshland et al., 1982).

claim: Bacteria modulate flagellar motion according to changes in the local nutrient concentration.
source_text: Prominent examples include the modulation of flagellar motion operated by bacteria according to changes in the local nutrient concentration
evidence_reasoning: This is a well-established example of bacterial chemotaxis, supported by citations (Tu et al., 2008; Tu, 2008; Mattingly et al., 2021).

claim: A key observation shared by most studies is the role of a negative feedback mechanism to induce emergent adaptive responses.
source_text: An observation shared by most of these studies is the key role of a negative feedback mechanism to induce emergent adaptive responses
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis of findings from multiple cited studies (Kollmann et al., 2005; De Ronde et al., 2010; Selimkhanov et al., 2014; Barkai and Leibler, 1997).

claim: Any information-processing system, biological or not, must obey information-thermodynamic laws that prescribe the necessity of a storage mechanism.
source_text: Moreover, any information-processing system, biological or not, must obey information-thermodynamic laws that prescribe the necessity of a storage mechanism
evidence_reasoning: This is a fundamental principle from information thermodynamics, supported by citation (Parrondo et al., 2015).

claim: The storage of information during processing generally requires energy.
source_text: As the storage of information during processing generally requires energy
evidence_reasoning: This is a fundamental principle from thermodynamics of computation, supported by citations (Bennett, 1982; Sagawa and Ueda, 2009).

claim: Sensing mechanisms have to take place out of equilibrium.
source_text: sensing mechanisms have to take place out of equilibrium
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical requirement for information processing, supported by multiple citations (Gnesotto et al., 2018; Hartich et al., 2015; Skoge et al., 2013; Lestas et al., 2010).

claim: The discovery of memory molecules hinted at the possibility that storing mechanisms might be instantiated directly at the molecular scale.
source_text: Recently, the discovery of memory molecules (Coultrap and Bayer, 2012; Frankland and Josselyn, 2016; Lisman et al., 2002) hinted at the possibility that storing mechanisms might be instantiated directly at the molecular scale.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from experimental discoveries of memory molecules, supported by citations.

claim: Negative feedback, storage, and out-of-equilibrium conditions seem to be necessary requirements for a system to process environmental information and act accordingly.
source_text: Overall, negative feedback, storage, and out-of-equilibrium conditions seem to be necessary requirements for a system to process environmental information and act accordingly.
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis and inference from multiple theoretical and experimental studies cited in the manuscript.

claim: In the presence of dynamic environments, it is common for a biological system to keep encountering the same stimulus.
source_text: Indeed, in the presence of dynamic environments, it is common for a biological system to keep encountering the same stimulus.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general observation about biological systems in natural environments.

claim: Under conditions of repeated stimuli, a progressive decay in the amplitude of the response is often observed, both at sensory and molecular levels.
source_text: Under these conditions, a progressive decay in the amplitude of the response is often observed, both at sensory and molecular levels.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the phenomenon of habituation, supported by general biological knowledge and citations.

claim: Habituation characterizes many neuronal circuits along the sensory-motor processing pathways in most living organisms, either invertebrates or vertebrates.
source_text: In particular, habituation characterizes many neuronal circuits along the sensory-motor processing pathways in most living organisms, either invertebrates or vertebrates
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the widespread occurrence of habituation, supported by citations (Malmierca et al., 2014; Shew et al., 2015).

claim: Inhibitory feedback mechanisms are believed to modulate the stimulus weight in neuronal circuits.
source_text: where inhibitory feedback mechanisms are believed to modulate the stimulus weight
evidence_reasoning: This is a current understanding in neuroscience, supported by citations (Lamiré et al., 2022; Fotowat and Engert, 2023; Barzon et al., 2025).

claim: The first complete characterization of habituating phenomena dates back to 1966.
source_text: Most importantly, the first complete characterization of habituating phenomena dates back to 1966 (Thompson and Spencer, 1966), when different hallmarks of habituation in vertebrate animals were characterized.
evidence_reasoning: This is a historical fact supported by citation to Thompson and Spencer, 1966.

claim: The connection between habituation in the animal kingdom and brainless molecular systems has only recently attracted considerable attention.
source_text: Despite its widespread occurrence across remarkably different scales, the connection between habituation in the animal kingdom and brainless molecular systems has only recently attracted considerable attention.
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation about recent trends in scientific research, implied by the context and recent citations.

claim: A limited number of dynamical models have been proposed to explore the similarities and differences between habituation in animal and molecular systems.
source_text: A limited number of dynamical models have been proposed to explore the similarities and differences between the manifestations of these two fundamentally distinct phenomena
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to recent modeling work (Eckert et al., 2024; Smart et al., 2024).

claim: Dynamical characterizations of habituation still lack a clear identification of the functional role of habituation in regulating information flow, optimal processing, and sensitivity calibration.
source_text: However, dynamical characterizations of habituation still lack a clear identification of the functional role of habituation in regulating information flow, optimal processing, and sensitivity calibration
evidence_reasoning: This identifies a gap in current understanding, supported by citation (Benda, 2021).

claim: The information gain peaks at intermediate levels of habituation.
source_text: We find that the information gain peaks at intermediate levels of habituation
evidence_reasoning: This is a key finding from the computational analysis presented in Figure 3.

claim: Optimal processing performances are necessarily tangled with maximal activity reduction.
source_text: uncovering that optimal processing performances are necessarily tangled with maximal activity reduction
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the analysis of information gain and habituation strength in the model.

claim: The region of optimal information gain can be retrieved by simultaneously minimizing dissipation and maximizing information in the presence of a prolonged stimulation.
source_text: This region of optimal information gain can be retrieved by simultaneously minimizing dissipation and maximizing information in the presence of a prolonged stimulation
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through Pareto optimization analysis in Figure 4.

claim: Several minimal models for adaptation are composed of three building blocks: one responsible for buffering the input signal, one representing the output, and one usually reminiscent of an internal memory.
source_text: Several minimal models for adaptation are composed of three building blocks (Ma et al., 2009; Tadres et al., 2022; Tu et al., 2008; Celani et al., 2011; Rahi et al., 2017): one responsible for buffering the input signal; one representing the output; and one usually reminiscent of an internal memory.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a common modeling framework, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The presence of two different transition pathways creates an internal non-equilibrium cycle in receptor dynamics.
source_text: Crucially, the presence of two different transition pathways, motivated by molecular considerations and pivotal in many energy-consuming biochemical systems (De Los Rios and Barducci, 2014; Astumian, 2019; Flatt et al., 2023), creates an internal non-equilibrium cycle in receptor dynamics.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the model's behavior, supported by citations to related biochemical systems.

claim: Without the storage population, the internal pathway would not be present and the receptor would satisfy an effective detailed balance.
source_text: Without the storage population, the internal pathway would not be present and the receptor would satisfy an effective detailed balance.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the model's behavior in the absence of storage.

claim: Active receptors transduce the environmental energy into an active pumping in the readout unit, allowing readout population to encode information on the external signal.
source_text: Active receptors transduce the environmental energy into an active pumping in the readout unit, allowing readout population to encode information on the external signal.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the mechanism by which the model encodes information.

claim: The presence of multiple timescales in the system is fundamental in shaping information between the different components.
source_text: As a final remark, we expect from previous studies (Nicoletti and Busiello, 2024a) that the presence of multiple timescales in the system will be fundamental in shaping information between the different components.
evidence_reasoning: This expectation is based on previous theoretical work, supported by citation.

claim: The biologically plausible assumption is that U undergoes the fastest evolution, while S and H are the slowest degrees of freedom.
source_text: Thus, we employ the biologically plausible assumption that U undergoes the fastest evolution, while S and H are the slowest degrees of freedom
evidence_reasoning: This assumption is described as biologically plausible and supported by citations (Celani et al., 2011; Ngampruetikorn et al., 2020).

claim: Habituation occurs when, upon repeated presentation of the same stimulus, a progressive decrease to an asymptotic level is observed in some parameters.
source_text: Habituation occurs when, upon repeated presentation of the same stimulus, a progressive decrease to an asymptotic level is observed in some parameters
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition of habituation supported by citations (Thompson and Spencer, 1966; Eckert et al., 2024).

claim: The model exhibits habituation in its strict sense, showing progressive decrease in response upon repeated stimulation.
source_text: In Figure 2a, we show that the system exhibits habituation in its strict sense.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by simulation results shown in Figure 2a.

claim: If the stimulus is paused and presented again after a short time, the system habituates more rapidly.
source_text: If the stimulus is paused and presented again after a short time, the system habituates more rapidly, that is the number of stimulations to habituate is reduced.
evidence_reasoning: This hallmark (potentiation) is demonstrated in Figure 2b.

claim: After waiting a sufficiently long time, the response can be fully recovered.
source_text: After waiting a sufficiently long time, the response can be fully recovered.
evidence_reasoning: This hallmark (spontaneous recovery) is demonstrated in Figure 2c.

claim: If the stimulation continues beyond habituation, the time to recover the response increases.
source_text: If the stimulation continues beyond habituation, the time to recover the response increases by an amount
evidence_reasoning: This hallmark (subliminal accumulation) is demonstrated in Figure 2d.

claim: Less intense stimuli result in stronger response decrements when normalized by the initial response.
source_text: When normalized by the initial response, less intense stimuli result in stronger response decrements
evidence_reasoning: This hallmark (input sensitivity) is demonstrated in Figure 2e.

claim: More frequent stimulation is associated with a more rapid and more pronounced response decrement.
source_text: By showing the responses up to the habituation time, we clearly notice that more frequent stimulation is associated with a more rapid and more pronounced response decrement.
evidence_reasoning: This hallmark (frequency dependence) is demonstrated in Figure 2h.

claim: Despite its simplicity and lack of biological details, the model encompasses the minimal ingredients to capture the main hallmarks defining habituation.
source_text: Summarizing, despite its simplicity and lack of biological details, our model encompasses the minimal ingredients to capture the main hallmarks defining habituation.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary conclusion based on the demonstrations in Figure 2.

claim: Habituation emerges due to the increase in the storage population, which provides increasing negative feedback to the receptor.
source_text: In our architecture, habituation emerges due to the increase in the storage population, which provides increasing negative feedback to the receptor and thus lowers the number of active readout units
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about the mechanism of habituation in the model, supported by the model dynamics.

claim: There exist parameters for which the mutual information when the system has habituated is larger than the initial mutual information.
source_text: Crucially, we find that there exist parameters for which IU,H(hab) is larger than IU,H(in).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the computational analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The information on H encoded by U in the habituated system is larger than the initial one for certain parameter values.
source_text: This result suggests that the information on H encoded by U in the habituated system is larger than the initial one.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the mutual information calculations shown in Figure 3.

claim: The mutual information gain displays a peak in an intermediate region of the (β,σ) plane.
source_text: In Figure 3c, we show that ΔIU,H displays a peak in an intermediate region of the (β,σ) plane.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly shown in Figure 3c.

claim: In the region of maximal information gain, the corresponding habituation strength attains intermediate values.
source_text: In this region, the corresponding habituation strength attains intermediate values, suggesting that too strong habituation can be detrimental
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in Figure 3d and interpreted as suggesting optimal intermediate habituation.

claim: The change in feedback information after habituation peaks in the same region as the mutual information gain.
source_text: Indeed, the change in feedback information after habituation, ΔΔIf=ΔIf(hab)−ΔIf(in), peaks in the same region of ΔIU,H
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Habituation promotes a decrease of the internal energy flux.
source_text: Habituation promotes a decrease of the internal energy flux
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in Figure 3f and 3k.

claim: The regime of maximal information gain supports habituation with a concurrent energetic advantage.
source_text: This observation suggests that the regime of maximal information gain supports habituation with a concurrent energetic advantage.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the combined analysis of information gain and energy flux.

claim: The Pareto optimal front in the (β,σ) plane qualitatively corresponds to the region of maximal information gain.
source_text: Remarkably, we find that the Pareto optimal front in the (β,σ) plane qualitatively corresponds to the region of maximal information gain
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in Figure 4b through comparison of the Pareto front with the information gain landscape.

claim: A system that has tuned its internal parameters to respond to a constant signal also learns how to respond optimally to the time-varying input of the same strength, in terms of information gain.
source_text: This implies that a system that has tuned its internal parameters to respond to a constant signal also learns how to respond optimally to the time-varying input of the same strength, in terms of information gain.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the correspondence between the Pareto front and maximal information gain region.

claim: The onset of habituation emerges spontaneously when the system attempts to activate its receptor as little as possible, while producing the minimum amount of storage molecules retaining enough information about the external environment.
source_text: Heuristically, the onset of habituation emerges spontaneously when the system attempts to activate its receptor as little as possible, while producing the minimum amount of storage molecules retaining enough information about the external environment.
evidence_reasoning: This is a heuristic interpretation of the optimization results.

claim: At low signal strengths, the Pareto front moves such that a larger storage cost σ is needed at fixed β.
source_text: We find that, at low ⟨H⟩max, the Pareto front moves in such a way that a larger storage cost σ is needed at fixed β.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in Figure 4c.

claim: At lower signal strengths, it is harder for the system to distinguish the input from the background thermal noise.
source_text: This is expected since, at lower signal strengths, it is harder for the system to distinguish the input from the background thermal noise.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference based on signal detection theory principles.

claim: If the system can adapt the inhibition strength κ to the value of the external signal, the Pareto fronts for different external signals collapse into a single optimal curve.
source_text: However, we can achieve a collapse of the optimal front if we allow the system to tune the inhibition strength κ to the value of the external signal
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated in Figure 4d.

claim: A system capable of adapting the negative feedback to its environment is able to always tune itself to the onset of habituation at different values of the external stimulus.
source_text: Thus, in this scenario, a system that is capable of adapting the negative feedback to its environment is also able to always tune itself to the onset of habituation at different values of the external stimulus and without tinkering with the energy cost σ
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the collapsed Pareto fronts shown in Figure 4d.

claim: The presence of a storage mechanism is fundamental in the model.
source_text: The presence of a storage mechanism is fundamental in our model.
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as a fundamental feature of the model architecture.

claim: The role of storage in mediating the negative feedback is suggested by several experimental and theoretical observations.
source_text: Furthermore, its role in mediating the negative feedback is suggested by several experimental and theoretical observations
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations (Celani et al., 2011; Tu et al., 2008; Kollmann et al., 2005; etc.).

claim: Whenever the storage is eliminated from the model, habituation cannot take place.
source_text: Whenever the storage is eliminated from our model, habituation cannot take place, highlighting its key role in driving the observed dynamics
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as a result from model analysis (details in Supplementary Information).

claim: The degree of habituation and the change in the storage population are deeply related to one another.
source_text: In Figure 5a, we show that the degree of habituation, Δ⟨U⟩, and the change in the storage population, Δ⟨S⟩, are deeply related to one another.
evidence_reasoning: This relationship is demonstrated in Figure 5a.

claim: The more the storage population relaxes between two consecutive signals, the less the readout population reduces its activity.
source_text: The more ⟨S⟩ relaxes between two consecutive signals, the less the readout population reduces its activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Increasing the interval between consecutive signals decreases the mutual information on the next stimulus.
source_text: Indeed, increasing ΔT, we observe a decrease of the mutual information (Figure 5b) on the next stimulus.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The proposed model is fully Markovian in its microscopic components.
source_text: We remark here that the proposed model is fully Markovian in its microscopic components
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the mathematical structure of the model.

claim: The memory that governs readout habituation spontaneously emerges from the interplay among the internal timescales.
source_text: and the memory that governs readout habituation spontaneously emerges from the interplay among the internal timescales
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about how memory emerges in the model despite its Markovian nature.

claim: The storage needs to evolve on a slower timescale, comparable to that of the external input, in order to generate information in the receptor and in the readout.
source_text: In particular, recent works have highlighted that the storage needs to evolve on a slower timescale, comparable to that of the external input, in order to generate information in the receptor and in the readout
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to previous work (Nicoletti and Busiello, 2024a).

claim: An instantaneous negative feedback implemented directly by U would lead to no time-dependent modulations of the readout and thus no habituation.
source_text: To strengthen our conclusions, we remark that an instantaneous negative feedback implemented directly by U (bypassing the storage mechanism) would lead to no time-dependent modulations of the readout and thus no habituation
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about an alternative model configuration (details in Supplementary Information).

claim: In neural systems, habituation is typically measured as a progressive reduction of the stimulus-driven neuronal firing rate.
source_text: In neural systems, habituation is typically measured as a progressive reduction of the stimulus-driven neuronal firing rate
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about neural habituation, supported by citations (Malmierca et al., 2014; Shew et al., 2015; Benda, 2021; etc.).

claim: The model can be extended to qualitatively reproduce some features of the progressive decrease in neuronal response amplitudes.
source_text: Our model can be extended to qualitatively reproduce some features of the progressive decrease in neuronal response amplitudes.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through comparison with zebrafish data in Figure 6.

claim: The patterns of the model-generated activity are remarkably similar to the experimental ones.
source_text: The patterns of the model-generated activity are remarkably similar to the experimental ones
evidence_reasoning: This is shown through comparison in Figure 6a.

claim: The first principal component accounts for the evoked neural response, while the second PC mostly reflects the habituation dynamics in experimental data.
source_text: This procedure reveals that the first principal component (PC) accounts for the evoked neural response, while the second PC mostly reflects the habituation dynamics.
evidence_reasoning: This is shown through PCA analysis of experimental data in Figure 6b.

claim: The model is able to capture the main features of the observed neural habituation, without the need for biological details.
source_text: This shows that our model is able to capture the main features of the observed neural habituation, without the need for biological details.
evidence_reasoning: This is concluded from the comparison between model and experimental PCA results in Figure 6.

claim: The model serves as a microscopic and archetypal description of sensing processes across biological scales.
source_text: In this work, we studied a minimal architecture that serves as a microscopic and archetypal description of sensing processes across biological scales.
evidence_reasoning: This is a characterization of the model's purpose and scope.

claim: The model robustly reproduces the hallmarks associated with habituation in the presence of a single type of repeated stimulation.
source_text: we have shown that our model robustly reproduces the hallmarks associated with habituation in the presence of a single type of repeated stimulation
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the results shown in Figure 2.

claim: Optimal systems lie at the onset of habituation, characterized by intermediate levels of activity reduction.
source_text: In particular, optimal systems lie at the onset of habituation, characterized by intermediate levels of activity reduction
evidence_reasoning: This is concluded from the Pareto optimization analysis in Figure 4.

claim: Both too-strong and too-weak negative feedback are detrimental to information gain.
source_text: as both too-strong and too-weak negative feedback are detrimental to information gain
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the peak in information gain at intermediate habituation levels shown in Figure 3.

claim: The functional advantages of the onset of habituation are rooted in the interplay between energy dissipation and information gain.
source_text: Our results suggest that the functional advantages of the onset of habituation are rooted in the interplay between energy dissipation and information gain
evidence_reasoning: This is a synthesis and interpretation of the Pareto optimization and information gain results.

claim: The general features of optimal habituation are tightly linked to the internal mechanisms to store information.
source_text: and its general features are tightly linked to the internal mechanisms to store information
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the role of storage in the model and its impact on information dynamics.

claim: It is generally accepted that inhibitory feedback mechanisms modulate the stimulus weight in neural habituation.
source_text: Although minimal, our model can capture basic features of neural habituation, where it is generally accepted that inhibitory feedback mechanisms modulate the stimulus weight
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation (Lamiré et al., 2022).

claim: Recent works reported the existence of a separate inhibitory neuronal population whose activity increases during habituation.
source_text: Remarkably, recent works reported the existence of a separate inhibitory neuronal population whose activity increases during habituation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation (Fotowat and Engert, 2023).

claim: The separate inhibitory neuronal population might play the role of a storage mechanism in neural habituation.
source_text: Our model suggests that this population might play the role of a storage mechanism, allowing the system to habituate to repeated signals.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation connecting the model to experimental observations.

claim: In neural systems, a prominent role in encoding both short- and long-term information is played by synaptic plasticity as well as by memory molecules.
source_text: However, in neural systems, a prominent role in encoding both short- and long-term information is also played by synaptic plasticity (Abbott and Nelson, 2000; Martin et al., 2000) as well as by memory molecules (Coultrap and Bayer, 2012; Frankland and Josselyn, 2016; Lisman et al., 2002), at a biochemical level.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about neural information encoding, supported by multiple citations.

claim: A comprehensive analysis of how information is encoded and retrieved will most likely require all these mechanisms at once.
source_text: A comprehensive analysis of how information is encoded and retrieved will most likely require all these mechanisms at once.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: The minimal architecture may provide crucial insights into the functional advantages of habituation in a wide range of biological systems.
source_text: Overall, the present results hint at the fact that our minimal architecture may provide crucial insights into the functional advantages of habituation in a wide range of biological systems.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative conclusion about the broader implications of the work.

claim: Understanding the information-theoretic performance of real-world biochemical networks exhibiting habituation remains a fascinating perspective to explore.
source_text: More generally, understanding the information-theoretic performance of real-world biochemical networks exhibiting habituation remains a fascinating perspective to explore.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The possibility of inferring the underlying biochemical structure from observed behaviors is a fascinating direction.
source_text: Upon these premises, the possibility of inferring the underlying biochemical structure from observed behaviors is a fascinating direction
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about future research, with reference to related work (Rahi et al., 2017).

claim: Incorporating multiple receptors or storage populations may be needed to harvest information in complex conditions.
source_text: To this end, incorporating multiple receptors or storage populations may be needed to harvest information in complex conditions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about potential model extensions.

claim: Correlations between external signals may help reduce the encoding effort.
source_text: In such scenarios, correlations between external signals may help reduce the encoding effort as, intuitively, S is acting as an information reservoir for the system.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative inference about how the model might behave with correlated signals.

claim: Stored information could be used to make predictions on future stimuli and behavior.
source_text: Moreover, such stored information could be used to make predictions on future stimuli and behavior
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about potential functions of stored information, with citations to related work (Bueti et al., 2010; Sederberg et al., 2018; Palmer et al., 2015).

claim: Both storage mechanisms and their associated negative feedback will remain core modeling ingredients for understanding biological information processing.
source_text: We believe that both storage mechanisms and their associated negative feedback will remain core modeling ingredients.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about the importance of these mechanisms in future models.

claim: The work encapsulates key ingredients to support habituation while still being minimal enough to allow for analytical treatment.
source_text: On the one hand, it encapsulates key ingredients to support habituation while still being minimal enough to allow for analytical treatment.
evidence_reasoning: This is a characterization of the model's balance between simplicity and biological relevance.

claim: The model may help the experimental quest for signatures of these physical ingredients in a variety of systems.
source_text: On the other hand, it may help the experimental quest for signatures of these physical ingredients in a variety of systems.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about potential experimental applications of the theoretical framework.

claim: Habituation may stem from an information-based advantage.
source_text: Ultimately, our results show how habituation – a ubiquitous phenomenon taking place at strikingly different biological scales – may stem from an information-based advantage
evidence_reasoning: This is a key conclusion drawn from the information-theoretic analysis of the model.
